findings.before: the position (of the body, a stance)
findings.after: the position (posture; rank in a firm)
findings.why: 'a stance' is answerable with die Einstellung (attitude, Haltung), whose clue is 'the attitude'. The example also uses the rank sense (wichtige Stellung in der Firma), which the clue did not cover.

findings.before: to record (a song); to take in (a person)
findings.after: to record (a song); to admit (into a club, a hospital)
findings.why: 'to take in' is also the second gloss of einnehmen ('to take in (money)') on the same B1 board. The first gloss disambiguates, but 'admit' removes the overlap.

findings.before: to interpret (a law); to lay out
findings.after: to interpret (a law); to lay out (goods, a floor)
findings.why: A bare 'to lay out' also fits darlegen (lay out your reasons), which shares the B2 board and has the clue 'to set out, to explain'. Adding an object keeps the two apart.

findings.before: I am leaving the bike in the courtyard.
findings.after: I park my bike in the courtyard.
findings.why: The clue says 'to park (a bike)'. The translation should match the clue's sense and the plain meaning of abstellen here.

findings.before: Who has changed my seat setting?
findings.after: Who has moved my seat?
findings.why: Raised in round 1 and not applied. 'changed my seat setting' is unnatural English, and the new clue now says 'move out of place (a seat …)'.

findings.before: Der Bote stellt das Paket morgen zu.
findings.after: Der Paketbote stellt das Paket morgen zu.
findings.why: Raised in round 1 and not applied. Bare 'der Bote' sounds dated or literary. exEn stays: 'The courier will deliver the parcel tomorrow.'

findings.before: Learn it as a word. be- makes the thing you order the direct object: Ich bestelle eine Pizza.
findings.after: Learn it as a word.
findings.why: Raised in round 1 and not applied. stellen already takes a direct object, so the second sentence explains nothing.

findings.before: A solution is quite conceivable.
findings.after: A solution is entirely conceivable.
findings.why: durchaus = entirely or certainly. British 'quite' often reads as 'fairly', which weakens the German.

findings.before: I'm just folding the laundry.
findings.after: I still have to fold the laundry.
findings.why: 'Ich lege noch die Wäsche zusammen' means the folding is still to be done (noch), not that it is happening right now.

findings.before: adj
findings.after: adv
findings.why: The id says .adv and the example uses it as an adverb (Grundsätzlich bin ich dafür), but the label now says adj. Either label it adv or make the id .adj; it is both in German.

findings.before: C1
findings.after: B2
findings.why: Raised in round 1. einen Kurs belegen and belegtes Brötchen are everyday B1/B2 German.

findings.before: ist angegangen
findings.after: hat/ist angegangen
findings.why: Still not applied, only the note was added. The header still teaches 'ist angegangen' for the lead sense (concern), whose Perfekt is 'Das hat dich nichts angegangen'. The new note now contradicts the header.

findings.before: hat/ist hat/ist gezogen
findings.after: hat/ist gezogen
findings.why: The fix was applied twice, so the line now reads 'hat/ist hat/ist gezogen'. This is a broken helper/Partizip display.

findings.before: to meet (someone) halfway; to come towards
findings.after: to meet (someone) halfway; to come the other way
findings.why: 'to come towards' is exactly what zukommen means ('auf jemanden zukommen'; its en reads 'come towards'), and both are on kommen Board B2. A learner can answer the second half with zukommen. 'Come the other way' (Gegenverkehr kommt entgegen) belongs only to entgegenkommen.

findings.before: to take away, to revoke (a licence)
findings.after: to revoke (a licence); to deprive (someone of)
findings.why: 'to take away' is also abziehen ('take away' = subtract or deduct: 'zehn abziehen'), and abziehen is on the same Board B2. 'Withdraw' would clash with zurückziehen, also on that board. 'Revoke' and 'deprive' lead only to entziehen.

findings.before: bring up (a child); wind up (a clock)
findings.after: wind up (a clock); bring up, raise (children, animals); tease
findings.why: The clue was changed to 'to wind up (a clock); to raise (an animal); to tease', but the meaning was not. The learner is now clued with two senses ('raise an animal', 'tease': 'jemanden aufziehen') that the card's meaning never states, and the clue order no longer matches the meaning.

findings.before: to walk up to (auf jemanden); to lie ahead (auf uns)
findings.after: to come up to (auf jemanden); to lie ahead (auf uns)
findings.why: 'walk up to' is the gehen verb ('auf jemanden zugehen', which is zugehen's clue in the gehen family). kommen = come.

findings.before: to arise; to pay for (für etwas)
findings.after: to arise (doubts, wind); to pay for (für etwas)
findings.why: A bare 'to arise' is close to vorkommen's 'to happen, to occur'. A typical subject makes it unambiguous.

findings.before: the access (to the internet, a building)
findings.after: the access (to the internet, to data)
findings.why: Der Eingang ('the entrance') is on the same B1 board. 'Access to a building' invites Eingang. Internet and data access are Zugang only.

findings.before: The deadline for the term paper is Friday.
findings.after: The term paper has to be handed in on Friday.
findings.why: The new translation drops the noun's meaning (handing in) and introduces 'deadline' (Abgabetermin), which the German does not say.

findings.before: give up; post (a parcel); place (an ad)
findings.after: give up; post (a parcel); set (homework, a task); place (an ad)
findings.why: Still not applied. Die Aufgabe (now grade M) comes from this missing 'set (homework)' sense: 'Hausaufgaben aufgeben'.

findings.before: nach = behind: give way and fall in behind.
findings.after: nach = after: you give way after pushing back, and yield to pressure (a floor or rope also gibt nach).
findings.why: Still not applied. 'Fall in behind' is a made-up picture and does not explain 'give in'.

findings.before: C1
findings.after: B2
findings.why: Still not applied. 'Daraus ergibt sich' and 'Die Studie ergab' are standard B2 reading.

findings.before: result in; sich ergeben: arise; surrender
findings.after: yield, show, come to (Die Umfrage ergab …); sich ergeben: arise, follow (from); surrender
findings.why: Still not applied. Without sich, ergeben means 'yield, show, come to'. 'Result in' is a loose fit.

findings.before: Mit Englisch kommt man hier gut durch.
findings.after: Hier ist so viel Verkehr, wir kommen nicht durch.
findings.why: The example shows 'get by', but the clue teaches 'get through (a crowd, an exam)'. 'Get by' also overlaps with auskommen's clue.

findings.before: You can get by here with English.
findings.after: There is so much traffic here, we can't get through.
findings.why: Matches the new example.

findings.before: Der Dieb entkommt durch das Fenster.
findings.after: Der Dieb ist durch das Fenster entkommen.
findings.why: A one-off escape is reported in the Perfekt. The Perfekt also shows the sein helper.

findings.before: The thief escapes through the window.
findings.after: The thief escaped through the window.
findings.why: Matches the new example.

findings.before: come later, follow
findings.after: come later, follow; comply with (einer Bitte nachkommen)
findings.why: Still not applied. 'Comply with' is the frequent written sense, and it cannot be derived from 'come later'.

findings.before: sich beziehen auf: refer to; das Bett beziehen: put sheets on
findings.after: sich beziehen auf: refer to; receive (Gehalt, Rente beziehen); das Bett beziehen: put sheets on
findings.why: Still not applied. 'Rente/Gehalt beziehen' is a high-frequency sense.

findings.before: I am writing about your advertisement.
findings.after: I am writing with reference to your advertisement.
findings.why: Keeps 'refer' visible in the translation.

findings.before: draw (curtains) closed
findings.after: draw (curtains) closed; sich etwas zuziehen: catch (an illness), sustain (an injury)
findings.why: Still not applied. Common B2 sense that cannot be derived from the curtains.

findings.before: to be dropped, to disappear (jobs, a reason; everyday word)
findings.after: to be cut, to disappear (jobs, benefits; not formal)
findings.why: 'to be dropped' is the first sense in entfallen's own meaning ('be dropped; slip your mind'), and 'a reason' works with entfallen too (der Grund entfällt). Both verbs are on the B2 board, so a learner can answer entfallen. Jobs and benefits are typical of wegfallen.

findings.before: to retain, to keep up (a habit, a system)
findings.after: to keep up, to stick with (a habit, a system)
findings.why: 'to retain' is a standard gloss of behalten (to keep), so the clue lets a learner answer behalten. 'Stick with / keep up' only fits beibehalten.

findings.before: the saying, a slogan
findings.after: the slogan, a catchy line (on a card or a T-shirt)
findings.why: 'the saying' is the normal gloss of das Sprichwort (proverb, saying), a form in the same family. Leading with slogan / catchy line points only to Spruch.

findings.before: to hold out, to keep going
findings.after: to keep going, not to give up (to the end)
findings.why: aushalten's own `why` glosses it as 'hold out', so 'hold out' points to both verbs. They are on different boards (B2 has no aus tile), so on boards this is only a risk outside a board.

findings.before: aus = out, to the end: hold out.
findings.after: aus = to the end: you bear something until it is over.
findings.why: 'hold out' is durchhalten's clue; using it to explain aushalten blurs the two verbs.

findings.before: Der Bus hält hier nicht an.
findings.after: Können Sie hier bitte kurz anhalten?
findings.why: For a bus at its stops natives say 'Der Bus hält hier nicht'. anhalten is typically a driver or car coming to a stop. The example also repeats the base-verb example (Der Bus hält ...).

findings.before: The bus does not stop here.
findings.after: Could you stop here for a moment, please?
findings.why: Matches the new example.

findings.before: to take notes (in class)
findings.after: to take notes (while someone is speaking)
findings.why: aufschreiben is on the same A2/B1 boards, and 'take notes in class' could be answered with it. 'while someone is speaking' is what mit- adds.

findings.before: I have a talk with my boss tomorrow.
findings.after: I'm having a talk with my boss tomorrow.
findings.why: 'I have a talk' reads as non-native English for a planned event; the present progressive is natural.

findings.before: What a coincidence that we meet here!
findings.after: What a coincidence that we're meeting here!
findings.why: Natural English uses the progressive for this one-off event.

findings.before: B2
findings.after: B1
findings.why: Copying homework is everyday school language; B1. Raised in round 1 and not applied.

findings.before: to check (in a book or a list)
findings.after: to check, to look something up (in a dictionary)
findings.why: The A2 board carries the durch tile, and durchsehen ('look through, check') fits 'check (in a list)' just as well (eine Liste durchsehen). 'Look it up in a dictionary' points only to nachsehen and stays distinct from aufsehen ('raise your eyes').

findings.before: to foresee (an end); to refrain (from)
findings.after: to see the end coming (nicht abzusehen); to refrain (von)
findings.why: Taken literally, 'to foresee' is vor + sehen, and vorsehen's own why says 'seen in advance', so a learner would build vorsehen. Anchoring the clue to the fixed phrase removes the clash.

findings.before: to provide, to fit (with something)
findings.after: to equip, to fit (mit: rooms with a TV)
findings.why: vorsehen's clue also starts 'to provide for', so the two ver-/vor- verbs could swap. 'equip ... mit' points only to versehen.

findings.before: to provide for, to plan (what a plan or law lays down)
findings.after: to plan for, to include (as a rule or schedule does)
findings.why: Drops 'provide', which clashes with versehen, and the doubled 'plan'. Matches the example (Der Plan sieht eine Pause vor = includes).

findings.before: vor = before: seen in advance.
findings.after: vor = ahead: what a plan sets out in advance.
findings.why: 'seen in advance' suggests 'foresee' (vorhersehen), which vorsehen does not mean, and pushes learners towards vorsehen for absehen's clue.

findings.before: the visibility (in fog); the view (from a seat)
findings.after: the visibility (in fog, on the road)
findings.why: The added 'the view' clashes with die Aussicht ('the view (from a window)'). 'view from a seat' could equally be Aussicht, and Aussicht's clue could in turn be answered with Sicht. Keep Sicht to visibility only.

findings.before: to look at; to watch (a film)
findings.after: to look at (someone); to watch (a film, sich)
findings.why: On the A2 board zusehen ('to watch (someone doing ...)') and fernsehen ('watch TV') also say 'watch'. Adding 'sich' and the plain 'look at someone' sense separates it.

findings.before: sich etwas ansehen: look at, watch
findings.after: look at (jemanden ansehen); sich etwas ansehen: have a look at, watch
findings.why: Not applied from round 1: the most frequent transitive sense (Sie sah mich an) is missing.

findings.before: Sie sieht vom Buch auf.
findings.after: Sie sieht von ihrem Buch auf.
findings.why: The exEn says 'her book' but the German says 'vom Buch'. 'von ihrem Buch' is also more natural. exEn stays 'She looks up from her book.'

findings.before: realise, accept
findings.after: realise, accept (a mistake); inspect (files: Akten einsehen)
findings.why: Not applied from round 1. The access sense also underlies die Einsicht 'access (to files)'.

findings.before: ersehen; besehen; hinsehen; wegsehen
findings.after: ersehen; besehen; hinsehen; wegsehen; die Nachsicht (leniency); die Durchsicht (check-through); durchsichtig (transparent); einsichtig (reasonable)
findings.why: Not applied from round 1. The boards can build these (B1 nach+t; B2 durch/ein + t (+ig)), and all are common DWDS words.

findings.before: to set off (on a trip)
findings.after: to start driving, to get going (at last)
findings.why: On the B1 board abfahren ('to depart, to leave') fits 'set off on a trip' just as well (Wir fahren morgen früh ab). wegfahren ('go away') also fits a trip. 'Start driving, get going' points to los = start.

findings.before: to depart, to leave (a train)
findings.after: to depart (a train, at the time on the timetable)
findings.why: 'to leave' also fits wegfahren (A2 board) and losfahren (the los tile is on the A2 board). Tie the clue to departure times.

findings.before: to run over; to run (a red light)
findings.after: to run over (the wheels go over it); to run a red light
findings.why: On the B2 board umfahren (separable) is 'to knock over (with a car)'. 'run over' and 'knock over/down with a car' swap easily, and einen Radfahrer umfahren is common German for knocking a cyclist down.

findings.before: to knock over (with a car)
findings.after: to knock down (a post, a bin) with a car
findings.why: Object examples (a post, a bin) keep it apart from überfahren (run over a person or animal).

findings.before: Are you coming with us?
findings.after: Are you coming along (with us)?
findings.why: 'Fährst du mit?' does not specify 'us', and the sense taught is 'ride along / get a lift'.

findings.before: The train departs at eight.
findings.after: The train's departure is at eight.
findings.why: The noun is the point of this form; the translation turns it back into the verb (abfahren).

findings.before: zerfahren; entfahren; widerfahren; anfahren; auffahren; ausfahren
findings.after: zerfahren; entfahren; widerfahren; anfahren; auffahren; ausfahren; die Überfahrt (crossing); die Durchfahrt (passage); die Weiterfahrt (onward journey); die Vorbeifahrt; der Mitfahrer (fellow passenger); die Mitfahrt
findings.why: Not applied from round 1. The boards (über/durch/weiter/vorbei/mit + t/er) build these everyday words.

findings.before: Ich bestehe die Prüfung.
findings.after: Ich habe die Prüfung bestanden!
findings.why: Not applied from round 1. The bare present is unnatural. New exEn: 'I passed the exam!'

findings.before: pass (an exam); bestehen aus: consist of
findings.after: pass (an exam); bestehen aus: consist of; bestehen auf: insist on; exist
findings.why: Not applied from round 1. These are high-frequency senses, and der Bestand's why relies on 'exist'.

findings.before: Ich widerstehe der Schokolade.
findings.after: Ich kann der Schokolade einfach nicht widerstehen.
findings.why: Not applied from round 1. The bare statement is stilted. New exEn: 'I just can't resist the chocolate.'

findings.before: the stall (at a market); a level, a state
findings.after: the stall (at a market); the level (der ... der Dinge)
findings.why: 'a state' overlaps with der Zustand ('the condition, the state (of a car)'). The first half already disambiguates, but the overlap should go.

findings.before: erstehen; anstehen; zustehen
findings.after: erstehen; anstehen; zustehen; der Aufstand (uprising); der Ausstand (strike); der Überstand (overhang); umständlich (complicated); beständig (constant); die Beständigkeit; verständig (sensible); geständig (has confessed); widerständig
findings.why: Not applied from round 1. The B1/B2 boards build these, and umständlich, beständig and Aufstand are very common.

findings.before: the qualification (school or university); the end
findings.after: the qualification (a school or university degree)
findings.why: The added 'the end' clashes with der Schluss ('the end (of a film, a meeting)') on the same A2 and B1 boards, and der Abschluss einer Sitzung is valid German, so the two clues swap.

findings.before: the end (of a film, a meeting)
findings.after: the end (of a film, a story)
findings.why: '(of a meeting)' also fits Abschluss and Schließung (Schließung der Sitzung). A film or story ending is plainly Schluss.

findings.before: to connect (a device); to join (sich)
findings.after: to connect (a printer); to join (sich, a group)
findings.why: 'join (sich)' is close to sich zusammenschließen ('to join forces, to merge (sich)'). 'a group' makes it unambiguous.

findings.after: der Aufschluss (information, insight); der Einschluss (inclusion); die Erschließung (development); die Entschließung (resolution); die Einschließung; die Ausschließung
findings.why: Not applied from round 1. The boards build these real, common words (auf/ein + stem; er/ent + ung).

findings.before: to switch off; to arrange (a time)
findings.after: to switch off (the light, the TV)
findings.why: 'to arrange (a time)' can also be answered with abmachen (einen Termin abmachen), and abmachen's clue 'to agree on (a deal)' can be answered with ausmachen. Both are on Board B1. Switch-off is the main A2 sense and is unique.

findings.before: to fasten; to fix (a date)
findings.after: to fasten, to tie up (a boat)
findings.why: 'to fix (a date)' can also be answered with abmachen or ausmachen (einen Termin abmachen/ausmachen), and abmachen is on the same B2 board. Tying up a boat is unique to festmachen.

findings.before: Wir haben noch keinen Termin festgemacht.
findings.after: Wir haben das Boot am Steg festgemacht.
findings.why: Keeps the example in the sense the new clue asks for. New exEn: 'We tied the boat up at the jetty.'

findings.before: We haven't fixed a date yet.
findings.after: We tied the boat up at the jetty.
findings.why: Matches the new example.

findings.before: to comb (a whole area, a forest)
findings.after: to scan, to search over (the sky, the ground)
findings.why: 'den Wald durchsuchen' is the most common way to say 'comb a forest', and durchsuchen is on the same B2 board. absuchen alone fits scanning a surface (den Himmel, den Boden, den Horizont absuchen).

findings.before: Die Polizei sucht den ganzen Wald ab.
findings.after: Mit dem Fernglas sucht er den Horizont ab.
findings.why: A forest search is equally durchsuchen, so the new example uses the scanning sense that only absuchen has. New exEn: 'He scans the horizon with his binoculars.'

findings.before: The police are combing the whole forest.
findings.after: He scans the horizon with his binoculars.
findings.why: Matches the new example.

findings.before: bearable
findings.after: bearable (heat, pain)
findings.why: tragbar's `en` includes 'bearable', and tragbar is on the same B2 board. Heat and pain are only erträglich. tragbar is used for costs and situations.

findings.before: the number of (people, things)
findings.after: a number of (eine ___ von Fragen)
findings.why: 'die Zahl der Teilnehmer' is just as correct as 'die Anzahl der Teilnehmer', so the clue also fits die Zahl, which is on the same A2 and B2 boards. 'eine Anzahl von' (a number of, several) only takes Anzahl.

findings.before: to leave out (the sugar, a detail)
findings.after: to leave out (sugar, salt in a recipe)
findings.why: 'ein Detail auslassen' is very common, so 'leave out a detail' fits the family form auslassen too. Leaving out an ingredient is weglassen.

findings.before: the announcement (at a station)
findings.after: the PA message (e.g. about a delay)
findings.why: 'die Ansage am Bahnhof' is also normal German, and die Ansage is on the same B1 board (its `en` is 'announcement'). 'PA message' points to Durchsage, whose root sense is a message sent through the loudspeaker.

findings.before: to announce (over a loudspeaker)
findings.after: to pass a message over the PA (a delay)
findings.why: ansagen is on the same B2 board, and 'Der Fahrer sagt die Haltestelle an' is at least as common as 'durchsagen'. 'Pass a message over the PA' points to durch-.

findings.before: This fabric doesn't show dirt.
findings.after: This fabric is resistant to dirt.
findings.why: 'unempfindlich gegen Schmutz' means the fabric does not get dirty or damaged easily. 'Doesn't show dirt' means the dirt is not visible, which is a different claim.

findings.before: The skin becomes more sensitive with age.
findings.after: The skin's sensitivity increases with age.
findings.why: The current English drops the noun, so the learner cannot see Empfindlichkeit = sensitivity in the translation.

findings.before: to leave behind (a person, a car)
findings.after: to leave behind (luggage, a car)
findings.why: 'leave (a person)' is also in the verlassen clue. Removing 'a person' keeps the two apart.

findings.before: Die Regierung hat ein neues Gesetz erlassen.
findings.after: Die Stadt hat ein Rauchverbot erlassen.
findings.why: In Germany parliament passes laws (beschließen, verabschieden); a government or authority erlässt Verordnungen and Verbote. New exEn: 'The city has issued a smoking ban.'

findings.before: The government has passed a new law.
findings.after: The city has issued a smoking ban.
findings.why: Matches the new example. Also, 'passed' does not translate erlassen ('issued').

findings.before: verb |  (split field empty)
findings.after: verb | SPLITS
findings.why: Still not applied. blaumachen is separable (Ich mache blau; hat blaugemacht).

findings.before: to pay back (money you borrowed)
findings.after: to pay back (money to a friend)
findings.why: 'Repaying borrowed money' is also abzahlen, which is on the same B1 board. A friend points to a one-off repayment.

findings.before: editing; processing
findings.after: editing; handling (of a case, an application)
findings.why: On Board B1 die Bearbeitung and die Verarbeitung sit together; Verarbeitung's clue is 'the processing (of data, of food)'. While Bearbeitung is glossed 'processing' (and its exEn says 'Processing your application'), the learner is taught that both mean processing and the clue cannot separate them.

findings.before: Processing your application takes four weeks.
findings.after: It takes four weeks to deal with your application.
findings.why: Goes with the en fix: keep 'processing' for Verarbeitung only.

findings.before: to work through (a list of tasks)
findings.after: to clear (a backlog, a to-do list) task by task
findings.why: 'to work through' is the gloss of durcharbeiten ('work through (a book)'), which is on the same B2 board; 'eine Liste durcharbeiten' is good German, so the clue has two answers.

findings.before: Die Schüler erarbeiten das Thema in Gruppen.
findings.after: Sie hat sich ihren guten Ruf hart erarbeitet.
findings.why: The new clue asks for 'earn by hard work (sich etwas: a reputation)', but the example still shows the 'work out a topic' sense. New exEn: 'She worked hard to earn her good reputation.'

findings.before: The pupils work on the topic in groups.
findings.after: She worked hard to earn her good reputation.
findings.why: Matches the new example.

findings.before: the reckoning (with the past)
findings.after: the coming to terms (with a country's past)
findings.why: 'reckoning' suggests Abrechnung (settling scores); Aufarbeitung is working through and coming to terms with the past.

findings.before: to go missing (a pet from its home)
findings.after: to run away (a pet; wording of 'missing' notices)
findings.why: 'Unsere Katze ist weggelaufen' is the everyday way to say a pet went missing, so weglaufen (same family; clue 'run away (from home)') answers this clue too. Point to the written, notice-style register that marks entlaufen.

findings.before: the division (of a country)
findings.after: the division (of Germany into East and West)
findings.why: On Board B2 die Aufteilung ('the split') also fits 'division of a country' (die Aufteilung Deutschlands in Zonen is common). The fixed historical term is 'die Teilung (Deutschlands)'; anchor the clue to it, matching the new example.

findings.before: As a self-employed yoga teacher, she has to do a lot of advertising.
findings.after: As a self-employed provider of yoga classes, she has to do a lot of advertising.
findings.why: 'Anbieterin von Yogakursen' is a provider of yoga classes, not a yoga teacher (Yogalehrerin); the translation hides the very word being taught.

findings.before: O
findings.after: M
findings.why: The new why shows ver-bieten = English for-bid, which is a single transparent step for an English speaker; 'Learn it as a word' and grade O now contradict the why.

findings.before: A bare stem with a vowel change, but das: an exception to learn.
findings.after: das: an + ge + bot; nouns built with ge- are mostly das (das Gebot, das Verbot).
findings.why: Now contradicts the revised notes on Gebiet, Gebot and Aufgebot, which explain das by the ge- formation.

findings.before: The breakdown of the talks surprised everyone.
findings.after: The breaking-off of the talks surprised everyone.
findings.why: Abbruch = deliberate breaking off/termination (as the clue says); 'breakdown' suggests Zusammenbruch, which is on the same B2 board.

findings.before: to find out by asking
findings.after: to obtain by asking (formal: opening hours, a price)
findings.why: 'Find out by asking' is exactly what nachfragen does in everyday German (ich frage mal nach); a learner can answer nachfragen. Mark the formal register and object.

findings.before: the follow-up question (to check)
findings.after: a query back to clarify (Bei ~n rufen Sie an)
findings.why: 'Follow-up question to check' is also die Nachfrage (auf Nachfrage = when asked again), and nachfragen's clue is 'to check by asking'. A learner can answer Nachfrage.

findings.before: to enquire, to ask formally (for an offer)
findings.after: to enquire formally (whether something is possible)
findings.why: The new example no longer involves an offer (… ob sie noch Termine frei haben); align the clue with it.

findings.before: to move on (to the next topic)
findings.after: to make the transition (to the next topic)
findings.why: 'Move on' reads as weiter (= on): a learner will build weiterleiten. überleiten is about leading across (transition), matching Überleitung.

findings.before: the distinction (between two things)
findings.after: the act of telling apart, making a distinction
findings.why: 'The distinction between two things' is also der Unterschied (Unterschied zwischen zwei Dingen = difference/distinction). A learner can answer Unterschied.

findings.before: to match, to agree (figures, opinions)
findings.after: to match, to tally (figures, two statements)
findings.why: 'To agree (opinions)' is also zustimmen ('to agree with'); a learner can answer zustimmen.

findings.before: the agreement, the match (between data)
findings.after: the match, the correspondence (between data)
findings.why: 'The agreement' is also die Zustimmung (consent, approval); a learner can answer Zustimmung.

findings.before: to come in (a room); to occur
findings.after: to come in, walk in (through the door)
findings.why: auftreten's clue is 'to perform (on stage); to occur'; both are on Board B1, so 'to occur' fits either. Also make it intransitive so betreten ('enter a room') on Board A2 doesn't fit.

findings.before: the cover (someone standing in)
findings.after: the cover arrangement (for an absent colleague)
findings.why: 'Someone standing in' is a person = der Vertreter (en: deputy, stand-in). A learner can answer Vertreter.

findings.before: to join, become a member (with the dative: einem Verein …)
findings.after: to join (+ dative, no 'in'): einem Verein …
findings.why: eintreten (in eine Partei eintreten) is a true synonym and is on the same B1 board; the only safe disambiguator is the construction, so make it explicit.

findings.before: Der Beitritt zum Verein ist kostenlos.
findings.after: Der Beitritt Polens zur EU erfolgte 2004.
findings.why: The clue now leads with 'accession (of a country to the EU)', but the example is about a club. New exEn: 'Poland joined the EU in 2004.'

findings.before: to prove (with documents); to detect
findings.after: to show proof of (income, with papers); to detect
findings.why: beweisen's clue is 'to prove (that something is true)'. Two clues that open with 'to prove' let a learner answer beweisen ('mit Dokumenten beweisen' is fine German).

findings.before: the instruction, order (given by the boss)
findings.after: the instruction (follow the ~s of the staff)
findings.why: The revision made it swap with die Weisung ('the directive (from a superior)'). Both clues now describe an order from above, so a learner can answer Weisung.

findings.before: to show, to have (faults, features)
findings.after: to exhibit, to have (defects, features of a thing)
findings.why: vorweisen's clue is 'to produce (a ticket); to have (experience)'. Both clues contain 'to show/to have'; tie aufweisen to properties of a thing.
